title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 8

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A thin piece of wood of uniform density in the shape of an equilateral triangle with side length \(3\) inches weighs \(12\) ounces. A second piece of the same type of wood, with the same thickness, also in the shape of an equilateral triangle, has side length \(5\) inches. Which of the following is closest to the weight, in ounces, of the second piece?

solutions.text:
Weight is proportional to area, and area scales with the square of the side length. The second side is \(\tfrac53\) times the first, so its weight is \(12\cdot\left(\dfrac53\right)^2=\dfrac{100}{3}\approx33.3\) ounces.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The weight is proportional to the area, which scales with the square of the side length
